title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2610.37613v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. Existing approaches maintain visual grounding during reasoning in two main ways: they either refer to evidence using textual coordinates, which specify symbolic locations rather than the visual content itself, or reinsert cropped regions or frames into the multimodal context, preserving visual details at the cost of substantial context expansion. To address these limitations, we introduce VideoLVR, which constructs latent visual evidence from local regions at relevant video moments, thereby providing visual support for intermediate reasoning steps. translated_title: VideoLVR：基于接地视频证据的潜在视觉推理
translated_abstract: 思维链推理极大地提升了多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的视频理解能力。然而，基于语言的推理轨迹并未提供一种可靠的机制让模型重新审视相关的视觉证据，从而导致视觉遗忘，并削弱模型对视频内容进行推理的能力。现有方法主要通过两种方式在推理过程中保持视觉接地：其一是使用文本坐标指代证据，但这只能指定符号化的位置而非视觉内容本身；其二是将裁剪的区域或帧重新插入多模态上下文中，虽保留了视觉细节，却以大幅扩展上下文为代价。为解决这些局限，我们提出了 VideoLVR，它从相关视频时刻的局部区域构建潜在视觉证据，从而为中间推理步骤提供视觉支持。为监督潜在视觉证据的生成，我们引入了一种……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: VideoLVR 通过从相关视频时刻的局部区域构建潜在视觉证据，为中间推理步骤提供视觉支持，在不大幅扩展上下文的前提下解决了视频推理中的视觉遗忘问题。
en_tdlr: VideoLVR constructs latent visual evidence from local regions at relevant video moments, providing visual support for intermediate reasoning steps and addressing visual forgetting in video reasoning without substantial context expansion.
